how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py logic (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed), run through .scratch/fetch_by_page.py because www.ssbwiki.com answers HTTP 403 to the reader's render call, which asks for the page by oldid; the wrapper asks for the same page by title and checks the revision the wiki returns. Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read at the revision named. SmashWiki pages cover every Smash game; a line states a Melee fact only where the page says so for Melee (the 'In Super Smash Bros. Melee' trophy text, a sentence naming Melee, or a Melee table column), or describes the item or enemy for the whole series without naming a game.

lines.line: Summary: A close-range item from Donkey Kong: grab it and you run across the screen swinging it back and forth nonstop. It is an extremely powerful item, but you have no recovery move while you carry it.

quoted: The Hammer (ハンマー, Hammer) is a close-range item that appears in all Super Smash Bros. games.
If you grab the Hammer, you'll run across the screen swinging it back and forth nonstop.
It's an extremely powerful item, but you have no recovery move when carrying it.
The hammer comes from the arcade game Donkey Kong.

lines.line: Uses: Grabbing it sends a player into a state that inflicts significant damage and knockback, but while swinging they cannot jump a second time in the air, use any other attacks or defend.

quoted: Upon being grabbed by any player, it sends them into a unique state that inflicts significant damage and knockback.
they will constantly swing the hammer back and forth, and will be unable to midair jump, use any other attacks, or defend

lines.line: Tips: Every now and then the mallet head falls off and the wielder ends up completely vulnerable, swinging just the handle; from Melee on there is a 12.5% chance of this as it is picked up, and the fallen Hammer Head can be picked up and thrown as a powerful item. If an opponent is swinging a Hammer, sending them off a ledge can effectively KO them, because they cannot use special moves or a midair jump unless they somehow drop the Hammer.

quoted: Every now and then, the mallet head will fall off, and you'll end up completely vulnerable, swinging just the handle.
Starting in Melee, there is a 12.5% chance (one out of eight) of the head of the Hammer falling off as it is picked up
The Hammer Head itself can be picked up and thrown as a powerful item.
As the wielder of the hammer cannot use special moves or midair jump, sending an opponent off a ledge while they swing the Hammer can effectively KO them unless they can somehow drop the Hammer.

lines.line: Summary: A long-range battering item, similar in appearance to a lightsaber. It can be wielded and charged for melee attacks or thrown, like all other battering items.

quoted: The Beam Sword (ビームソード, Beam Sword) is a long-range battering item.
It is similar in appearance to a lightsaber, and is often informally referred to as the "lightsaber" for this reason.
it can be wielded and charged for melee attacks or can be thrown, like all other battering items.

lines.line: Uses: As a battering item it bolsters your power and adds some options through throwing. The blade lengthens in direct proportion to the power of an attack, so it reaches its maximum size when swung as a smash attack, and the length changes depending on who wields it.

quoted: the Beam Sword will bolster the player's power, as well as potentially add some options to their game via throwing.
The blade also lengthens in direct proportion to the power of an attack, so it reaches its maximum size when swung as a smash attack.
but the length changes depending on who wields it.

lines.line: Looks like: A distinctive glowing blade that is at first about the size of a short sword.

quoted: With its distinctive glowing blade, the Beam Sword is eye-catching and lethal.
At first, the blade is about the size of a short sword

lines.line: Tips: In Melee its range significantly increases in size, particularly on charged smash attacks. Peach can pull a Beam Sword out with her Vegetable attack, but the chance is slim: 1/768 in Melee.

quoted: In Melee and Brawl, the Beam Sword's range significantly increases in size, particularly in the case of charged smash attacks.
In Melee and Brawl, a Beam Sword is one of few unusual items Peach can pull out via her Vegetable attack, though the chances of this are slim; 1/768 and 1/480 in Melee and Brawl respectively.

lines.line: Summary: A magic wand that holds 16 star shots and sends foes flying at a low angle when thrown. It works as an unusual combination of a battering item and a projectile item.

quoted: This magic wand holds 16 star shots and sends foes flying at a low angle when thrown.
the Star Rod acts as an unusual combination of both battering and projectile items.

lines.line: Uses: Hit opponents up close with it, or use smash attacks or tilts to shoot long-range stars that can hit from a distance. It is most powerful when Captain Falcon or Sheik performs a smash attack while holding it.

quoted: As a battering item, combatants can use the Star Rod to directly hit opponents up close.
Using either smash attacks or tilts, however, cause the Star Rod to shoot out long-range stars that can hit opponents from a distance
It's most powerful when Captain Falcon or Sheik performs a Smash Attack while holding it.

lines.line: Tips: The item has only sixteen stars, and Captain Falcon's smash attack shoots off 5 stars and Sheik's 2, so they use it up quickly. When it runs out, throwing it at enemies is the more practical option: a thrown Star Rod deals powerful semi-spike knockback that can gimp recoveries or act as a general KO move. The stars are projectiles, so they can be reflected or absorbed.

quoted: with Falcon's attacks shooting off 5 stars and Sheik's firing off 2 stars.
The item, however, has only sixteen stars, and using either of the two aforementioned characters can cause the item to quickly deplete its ammunition.

A more practical option, however, is to throw the item towards enemies; the Star Rod, when thrown, deals powerful semi-spike knockback, which can potentially gimp recoveries or act as a general KO move.
As the stars are considered projectiles by the game, they can be reflected by a variety of moves; in addition, they can also be absorbed.

lines.line: Summary: A long-range shooting item based on a Super Nintendo peripheral. In Melee, tapping the attack button fires three small shots, and holding it charges a stronger, larger shot.

quoted: is a shooting item that appears in Super Smash Bros. Melee, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, Super Smash Bros. 4, and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, based on a real-life peripheral from Nintendo.
Tapping the attack button will fire three small shots in Melee
Holding down the attack button charges the weapon, allowing for stronger and larger shots and having decent KO potential at full charge.

lines.line: Uses: Tap the attack button repeatedly for a constant stream of small shots that each do little knockback and damage; the high rate of fire gives a trapping effect, as the opponent has little or no time to act. Hold the button to charge a bigger shot. It has limited ammunition, 48 shots in Melee, and the higher charge levels use more.

quoted: If the player constantly taps the attack button, they will fire a constant stream of small shots, each of which does little knockback and damage.
The high rate of fire and low knockback causes a "trapping" effect as the opponent will have little-to-no time to act
The Super Scope has limited ammunition, with 48 shots in Melee and Brawl
Different charge levels will increase the ammo used.

lines.line: Tips: In Melee you could not move while shooting it. The uncharged shots pass through opponents, so a stream can trap several enemies, but their 280 degree knockback angle makes a very weak meteor smash that is ineffective against opponents close to the stage. When it runs out of ammunition it only fires a puff of smoke, and you can throw the weapon for a little extra knockback and damage.

quoted: In Super Smash Bros. Melee, you could not move while shooting it, but in this game, you can move and jump while blasting!
In Melee, the uncharged shots have a 280° knockback angle, resulting in a very weak meteor smash, making it ineffective against opponents close to the stage.
The uncharged shots can also pass through opponents, allowing it to trap multiple enemies

Attempting to use the Super Scope after it runs out of ammunition causes it to fire nothing but a puff of smoke — at this point, the player can throw the weapon at opponents for a little extra knockback and damage.

lines.line: Summary: A long-range weapon that is fairly weak, but since it fires so fast it can easily juggle enemies.

quoted: The Ray Gun (レイガン, Ray Gun) is a long-range weapon used in all games of the Super Smash Bros. series.
The Ray Gun is toy-like in appearance and shoots short, fat, highly reflective beams of green light.
The gun is fairly weak, but since it fires so fast, it can easily juggle enemies.

lines.line: Uses: It holds 16 shots. In Melee each shot deals 4% with horizontal knockback and can be fired every 30 frames, which lets it juggle opponents at low percents or carry them to the blast line at mid percents.

quoted: A Ray Gun can be shot 16 times before it runs out of ammunition.
In Super Smash Bros. Melee, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, and Super Smash Bros. 4 each shot deals 4% without electricity, horizontal knockback, and can be fired every 30 frames.
The horizontal knockback allows it to easily juggle opponents at low percents or to carry them to the blast line at mid percents.

lines.line: Looks like: Toy-like in appearance, with a fat shape, and it fires beams of green light.

quoted: The Ray Gun is toy-like in appearance and shoots short, fat, highly reflective beams of green light.

lines.line: Tips: The shots can be reflected or absorbed, while the gun itself, when thrown, can only be reflected. Try dropping it with a few shots left and watch your foes waste time and energy retrieving it.

quoted: The shots can be reflected or absorbed, while the gun itself (when thrown) can only be reflected.
Try dropping it with a few shots left and watch your foes waste time and energy retrieving it.

lines.line: Summary: The two healing items: each reduces the damage percentage of whoever picks it up. In Melee the Maxim Tomato heals 50% of a character's damage percentage and the Heart Container heals a total of 100%.

quoted: is a healing item (a red tomato with a black "M" in the center) first introduced in the Kirby series, which reduces the damage percentage of the player who picks it up.
Beginning in Super Smash Bros. Melee, the Maxim Tomato heals 50% from a character's damage percentage, with Heart Containers taking the previous function of healing 100% damage.
is an item that will reduce the damage of the character who picks it up.
Heart Containers function similarly to 64. However, it now only heals a total of 100%.

lines.line: Uses: After you eat a Maxim Tomato and a brief moment passes, your damage meter slowly drains the amount, whether or not you pick up another item right afterwards. Damage you take while healing is subtracted from what the tomato heals: if an attack does 10% damage, you only recover 40%. Heart Containers drift toward the ground slowly and replenish 100 percentage points of health.

quoted: Once you eat one, after a brief moment, your damage meter slowly drains the appropriate amount, regardless of whether or not you pick up another item right afterwards.
Also beginning in Melee, damage taken while healing will be subtracted from the amount healed by the tomato.
if an attack does 10% damage, the tomato will "absorb" it into its 50% recovery, and the user only recovers 40% damage.
Heart Containers drift toward the ground slowly and replenish 100 percentage points of health.

lines.line: Looks like: The Maxim Tomato is a small red tomato with a noticeable black and white M on the front.

quoted: The Maxim Tomato is a small red tomato, with a noticeable black and white M on the front.

lines.line: Tips: In the All-Star Rest Area you are given three Heart Containers that can heal all of your damage instead of the standard 100%. Due to a glitch, entering the teleporter in Melee interrupts a Heart Container's healing, so it does not fully heal you.

quoted: The player is given three Heart Containers in the All-Star Rest Area that can heal all of their damage instead of the standard 100%.
Due to a glitch, entering the teleporter in Melee will interrupt the Heart Container's healing and thus not fully heal the player.

lines.line: Summary: A transforming item that debuted in Melee: whoever breaks it becomes a Metal fighter for a short time, much heavier but slower and quicker to fall.

quoted: The Metal Box item debuted as a transforming item in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
The Metal Box transforms the player's fighter who breaks it into a Metal fighter.
Your mass is exponentially greater while metallic, making it difficult for others to throw you.
not only will you move a bit slower, but you'll also fall much more quickly than you ordinarily would.

lines.line: Uses: In Melee the effects last 12 seconds, though the time limit decreases as the fighter takes damage, especially from fire attacks. Weight is multiplied by 3.0 and walking speed by 0.7, while falling speed and gravity are both doubled.

quoted: The effects last 12 seconds, but the time limit decreases as the fighter takes damage, especially from fire attacks like Bowser's Fire Breath.
Increases the fighter's weight (3.0× in Melee; 4.5× in Brawl, Smash 4, and Ultimate)
Decreases the fighter's walking speed slightly (0.7× in Melee, Brawl, and Smash 4; 0.8× in Ultimate).
Increases the fighter's falling speed (2.0× in Melee and Brawl; 1.7× in Smash 4; 1.4× in Ultimate)
Increases the fighter's gravity slightly (2.0× in Melee and Brawl; 1.7× in Smash 4 and Ultimate).

lines.line: Tips: The faster fall makes recoveries harder. In Melee, a Metal Box hit by a projectile disappears, but disjointed attacks and any attack from a sword-wielding character still break it and still turn the attacker into a Metal fighter.

quoted: making recoveries harder and more vulnerable to certain chain grabs.
In Melee, if the Metal Box is broken by disjointed attacks like Pikachu's forward smash or any attack from a sword-wielding character, they will still transform them into a Metal fighter.
Also, if the Metal Box is hit by a projectile, it will disappear.

lines.line: Summary: An item from the Mario series, known as the Starman in Melee, that makes you invulnerable to all attacks for a short period of time.

quoted: The Super Star (スーパースター, Super Star), known as the Starman prior to the PAL release of Super Smash Bros. Brawl and the NTSC release of Super Smash Bros. 4, is an item from the Mario series.
This item makes you invulnerable to all attacks for a short period of time.

lines.line: Uses: All you need to do is touch it to power up. Melee repeats the first game's behaviour, where the fighter is invincible for ten seconds but does not damage opponents by touching them.

quoted: but all you need to do is touch it to power up.
The Starman returns as an item, reprising its behavior from Super Smash Bros.
The player's fighter will become invincible for ten seconds, but it doesn't damage the opponents when touched.

lines.line: Looks like: The fighter who grabs it is given a bright, sparkling appearance.

quoted: Also, the player's fighter will be given a bright, sparkling appearance

lines.line: Tips: It bounces around in large arcs and eventually tumbles out of the stage, so touch it before it falls off. In Melee its theme music lowers the stage music's volume until the stage music is extremely difficult to hear.

quoted: The Starman bounces around and eventually tumbles out of the stage
The Super Star bounces on the field and off platforms or walls in large arcs, and can fall off the stage if not grabbed in time
Unlike in the previous game, the Starman's theme music lowers the stage music's volume to the point that it becomes extremely difficult to hear over the layered theme.

lines.line: Summary: Two Mario items that change your size for about ten seconds. The Super Mushroom, which debuted in Melee, makes you giant, and the Poison Mushroom makes you shrink.

quoted: The Super Mushroom debuts as a transformation item, with the effects described above.
The transformation lasts about ten seconds.
The Poison Mushroom debuted as an effect item in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
in Super Smash Bros. Melee, they make you shrink on contact.

lines.line: Uses: The Super Mushroom raises your size, strength and mass, making it harder for foes to knock you off; in Melee it multiplies weight by 1.6 and the damage of direct attacks by 1.2, but gives no armor, so you still flinch from any knockback. The Poison Mushroom takes away power and mass, making you a prime target to get smashed offscreen with even a light attack.

quoted: In Super Smash Bros. Melee, they temporarily turn your character into a giant. Not only will your size and strength increase, but so will your mass, making it harder for foes to knock you off.
Increases the fighter's weight (applies a 1.6× multiplier in Melee
Increases the base power of direct attacks (1.2× in Melee
The item does not offer any armor, however, so the fighter will still flinch from attacks that deal any amount of knockback.
With your diminished stature comes a loss of power and mass, making you a prime target to get smashed offscreen with even a light attack.

lines.line: Looks like: The Poison Mushroom is a deceptive look-alike of the Super Mushroom, with a slightly darker coloration and angry eyes.

quoted: while also retaining the slightly darker coloration and angry eyes.
They are mushrooms that deceptively resemble the Super Mushroom, but with a duller color scheme and angry eyes.

lines.line: Tips: Both keep sliding to the right, but in Melee they slide left if they spawn on the right half of the stage. Touching one while under the effect of the other restores your normal size. In Melee, jumping at the moment a Super Mushroom's effects wear off gives a super jump almost as high as two jumps while wearing the Bunny Hood.

quoted: The Super Mushroom appears on the stage and keeps sliding to the right. In Super Smash Bros. Melee, it will slide left if it spawns on the right half of the stage.
Touching a Super Mushroom while under the effect of a Poison Mushroom and vice versa will restore a character to their normal size
In Melee, jumping at the moment that the Super Mushroom's effects wear off also causes characters to perform a super jump that is almost as high as two jumps while wearing the Bunny Hood.
It will appear on the stage and keeps sliding to the right. In Melee, it will slide left if it spawns on the right half of the stage.

lines.line: Summary: Common enemies in Melee's 1-player modes, in male and female varieties. Generally they are weak and light fighters and are very easy to KO.

quoted: are common enemies in various 1-player modes in Super Smash Bros. Melee.
Fighting Wire Frames come in male and female varieties
Generally, they are weak and light fighters, and are very easy to KO

lines.line: Weak points: They cannot use special moves or charge smash attacks, and their moves are much weaker versions of Captain Falcon's and Zelda's attacks; they make up for having no recovery moves with high jumping. Their attacks lack any real physical strength, and they are slow and easy to outmaneuver.

quoted: as to compensate their lack of recoveries due to their inability to use special moves, the Fighting Wire Frames have high jumping prowess.
They are also unable to charge smash attacks and their moves are much weaker versions of Captain Falcon and Zelda's attacks.
All Fighting Wire Frames lack the ability to use special techniques, and their attacks lack any real physical strength. Additionally, they're slow and are therefore easy to outmaneuver.

lines.line: Looks like: A framework of pink lines in a humanoid shape, with the Super Smash Bros. logo on the face and a red heart-like object in the chest; they are larger than the characters they are modelled on.

quoted: are, true to their name, a framework of pink lines in a humanoid shape
Their faces feature the Super Smash Bros. logo, and a red heart-like object can be found within their chests.
The Fighting Wire Frames are also larger than their counterparts

lines.line: Tips: Males always home towards your character, while females play a more passive role and rarely attack directly. In Cruel Melee all of them are extremely aggressive, extremely powerful and harder to knock off-stage, so characters cannot survive easily among them. In Adventure Mode they are fought in a low-gravity version of Battlefield, and there and in Multi-Man Melee they cannot be Star or Screen KO'd.

quoted: males always home towards the player's character, whereas the females tend to play a more passive role, rarely directly assaulting or attacking the player.
In Cruel Melee, however, all Wire Frames are extremely aggressive, and are also handicapped to be extremely powerful and harder to knock off-stage.
Characters cannot survive easily among the Wire Frames because of their amplified power and aggressive edge-guarding.
In Adventure Mode, the Fighting Wire Frames are fought in a low-gravity version of Battlefield.
In Adventure Mode and Multi-Man Melee, the Wire Frames have the property of being unable to be Star or Screen KO'd

lines.line: Summary: The last fight of Classic Mode, fought on the Melee version of Final Destination. It has a set amount of HP that must be depleted to win, and in Melee that amount depends on the difficulty.

quoted: He is the final boss of the 1-player Classic Mode, and has a set HP which must be depleted to win
He is fought on the Melee version of Final Destination.
His HP is now dependent on difficulty, instead of having 300 HP regardless of difficulty.

lines.line: Weak points: In Melee this boss loses the ability to turn around, and its movement depends entirely on the attack it is using and your position: it always returns to its starting position when it is not attacking.

quoted: he loses the ability to turn around
Master Hand's movement is now entirely dependent on the attack he's using and the player's position; he always returns to his starting position when not attacking.

lines.line: Looks like: A giant white glove; in Melee its wrist fades into nothingness instead of ending in a cuff.

quoted: just because it wears a white glove doesn't mean it fights clean.
instead of appearing as a glove with a "cuff", Master Hand's "wrist" fades into nothingness.

lines.line: Tips: Its power increases with each increment in difficulty, and the highest levels give it many attacks that can KO in one hit. Laser Nail shoots a laser beam from each fingertip; Finger Bullet fires one pair of bullets until it has taken 150% damage and three pairs after that. Power Slap buries the player, and the Vertical Throw cannot KO under normal conditions. Taking half of its HP off within the time limit brings a second boss into the fight.

quoted: In addition to this increase in HP, his power increases with each increment in difficulty, with the highest levels giving him a multitude of attacks with OHKO potential.
Master Hand shoots a laser beam from each of his fingertips.
He fires one pair if he hasn't taken 150% damage yet, and three pairs if he took 150% damage or more.
Master Hand slaps the ground. Buries the player.
High damage and knockback, but cannot KO under normal conditions.
If the player reduces Master Hand's HP by half, Crazy Hand appears

sections.name: A hidden boss in Classic Mode

lines.line: Summary: A bonus boss that appears in Classic Mode's last fight, alongside the final boss. To face it you must play on Normal difficulty or higher and reduce the final boss's HP by half within a total of 5 minutes and 50 seconds since the start of the mode.

quoted: In Classic Mode, he appears as a bonus boss fought alongside Master Hand; to fight him, one must play Classic Mode on Normal difficulty or higher, reach Master Hand, and reduce Master Hand's HP by half within a total of 5 minutes and 50 seconds since the start of the mode.

lines.line: Weak points: It starts with the same number of HP that the first boss started with, and you have only one chance to defeat it. Its Spasm attack cannot hit aerial targets, and a Finger Bomb that hits a character before it reaches the ground does only low damage with minimal knockback.

quoted: Crazy Hand starts with the same number of HP that Master Hand started with (dependent on the difficulty).
You have only one chance to defeat the Crazy Hand.
Very large hitbox and sends opponents upward, but cannot hit aerial targets.
If a bomb hits a character before it hits the ground, it does low damage with minimal knockback.

lines.line: Looks like: Its basic appearance is exactly the same as the final boss's, apart from being a left hand.

quoted: Crazy Hand's basic appearance is exactly the same as Master Hand's (apart from being a left hand)

lines.line: Tips: Most of its attacks are stronger variations of the final boss's, plus a few of its own. Flying Punch can star KO as low as 35%, the Forward Throw can KO at low percentages without DI, and the third poke of Tri-Poke can star KO at middle to high percentages.

quoted: Most of Crazy Hand's attacks are stronger variations of Master Hand's; however he also has a few unique attacks of his own.
star KOing as low as 35%.
KOing the player at low percentages without DI.
being capable of star KOing any players at middle to high percentage.
